title: Polymorphic Shotfarm — prompt rotation sandbox
content:
Context / intent:
- Trying a new mental model: treat exemplar collections like a greenhouse ("Shotfarm") where exemplars are propagated, mutated, and seasonally rotated to avoid overfitting to a narrow style.
- Goal: create a rotation policy and lightweight mutation ops that improve robustness across distribution shifts (tone, user goal mismatch, token budget constraints).
- This doc = playground scratchpad, rough drafts of templates + quick failure-cases catalog. Informal notes, experiments, TODOs.

Core ideas (short):
- Polymorphic exemplars: each exemplar (one-shot / few-shot block) is stored with metadata: domain, register, answer-length, anchor-tokens, fragility-score. Rotation picks exemplars with complementary anchors.
- Mutations: paraphrase exemplar prompts, swap synonyms, compress examples (truncate context), inject anti-examples (explicit failure case) to teach model to avoid certain responses.
- Rotation heuristics: diversity-first, recency-decay, fragility-penalty, user-segmentation bias correction.

Quick sketch: exemplar schema (informal)
- id: string tag (exp-001)
- short-label: "policy-suggestion-compact"
- domain: "payment-disputes"
- register: "concise/neutral"
- example: (short text block)
- anchors: ["chargeback","merchant"]
- fragility_score: 0.7 (0-1, higher = brittle)
- last_used: 2026-01-18
- performance_notes: "good for short answers, fails on multi-step reasoning"

Sample few-shot set (for customer-support tone normalization)
--- TEMPLATE (rotation slot A) ---
Instruction: You are a helpful assistant. For the examples below, produce a clear, 2-3 sentence answer, with one actionable next step.
Example 1 (Q): My account shows a duplicate charge from "Wigeon Co" for $24. When will I get refunded?
Example 1 (A): I’m sorry about that duplicate charge. I see a pending refund — you should receive funds in 3–5 business days; if not, reply and I’ll escalate to billing.
Example 2 (Q): I returned an order but didn’t get a refund.
Example 2 (A): Thanks for the heads up — can you share the return confirmation number? Once I have that, I’ll verify the refund status and follow up.
--- END TEMPLATE ---

Rotation note: slot A = anchor tokens {"refund","return","duplicate"}. When user contains any anchor, prefer slot A, else sample other slots. But also sometimes slot B (detailed troubleshooting) is better. Need soft selection (prob weights).

Mutation examples (quick ops):
- paraphrase-ex: run two paraphrases of answer, keep the shorter one if token budget < 120.
- compress-context: remove irrelevant preamble in examples (dates, account ids)
- anti-ex: add one negative example showing a bad answer and annotate why (e.g., overly technical)

Failure-case catalog (observed so far):
1) Hallucinated policy references: model cites "section 3.2" which doesn’t exist. Cause: exemplar included internal doc language. Fix: replace policy references with explicit quotes or remove.
2) Overly verbose on mobile UI: when user says "on mobile" assistant replies with full desktop steps. Fix: add mobile-specific exemplar and anchor tokens {"iOS","Android","mobile"}.
3) Defensive refusals: model says "I can't help with billing" after paraphrased prompt. Likely due to negative anti-ex present in rotation pool. Lower fragility_score or remove anti-example.
4) Token-bloated few-shot: concatenated examples exceed budget and triggers truncation mid-example — strategy: shard examples and prefer shorter answers for low-token deployments.

Experiments run (notes):
- exp-001: rotation naive-random vs diversity-first on synthetic user set (n=600).
  - model: redwood/gpt-small-v1 (local dedicated)
  - result: diversity-first reduced hallucination counts by ~18% but increased short-answer rate (need to tune weight).
- exp-002: paraphrase mutation with temperature=0.7 and then filter by length. Reduced token consumption by 9% but introduced slight tone drift (more casual). Tradeoff: add register anchor to maintain tone.
- exp-003: anti-ex injection to curb a specific bad behaviour (policy-citation). Successful in 4/5 tests, but produced brittle refusal in 2/20.

Notes to self / open questions:
- How to compute fragility_score cheaply? quick proxy: variance across N paraphrases' outputs on a small probe set.
- How frequently rotate vs cache exemplars? Maybe rotate per-user-session up to 3 swaps, then freeze to maintain coherence.
- Can we do per-route rotation policies in console? Need a config shape: route -> rotation-strategy-id -> seed-anchors. File a small product doc.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Formalize rotation policy config JSON (schema + minimal UI knobs).
- [ ] Run small A/B with Hosted API + token-cost logging (per-token breakdown).
- [ ] Pull a 200-example failure set from support logs (Ravi to help).
- [ ] Add mobile-specific exemplar slot and test on iOS flows.
- [ ] Prototype an offline mutation pipeline (paraphrase+compress) and store hashed variants to dedupe.

Quick snippets (copyable) — compact templates for play:
1) compact-instruction-template: "Answer in 2 sentences. Give one actionable next step. If unclear, ask one clarifying question."
2) fewshot-compact (2-shot): 
  Q: I was charged twice for a subscription.
  A: Sorry about that. I see duplicate charges sometimes clear automatically; please share your invoice number and I’ll verify and request a refund.
  Q: My promo code didn't apply.
  A: Thanks — can you share the code and the email used? I’ll check whether the promotion applied to your account.

Micro-observations:
- Shorter exemplars are more robust to token truncation but lose nuance. Might pair a short exemplar with a long optional one gated by available tokens.
- Anchor matching is brittle on synonyms; experiment with embedding-similarity fallback (cosine > 0.78).
- Store exemplar lineage (where it came from) — helps audit hallucination sources.

Scratch ideas for rotation algos (brain dump):
- diversity-first: maximize token-level n-gram dissimilarity across chosen exemplars.
- fragility-penalty: avoid exemplars with high fragility unless explicit override.
- reciprocal-sampling: pair complementary exemplars (concise + detailed) and randomly pick order to reduce positional bias.

Logs / quick provenance:
- pulled customer transcripts (anonymized) 2026-01-09 for initial seed.
- tested on dedicated cluster: eu-west-1-dedicated-2 on 2026-01-16 (runtime note: KV cache warmed fast but some tail latency spikes).

If you read this later: this is a working hypothesis. Keep it messy. When we polish for product, move to shared_drives/product/optimize/shotfarm-spec.md (link later).

Raw dump of a failing exchange (redacted):
USER: I returned my jacket two weeks ago, where is my refund?
ASSISTANT (bad): The policy states refunds are processed in 7–10 business days under section 4.2.
ASSISTANT (desired): Sorry about that — typically refunds take 7–10 business days. Can you share your return confirmation number so I can check? If you don’t have it, I’ll look up the order by email.
